overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that unchanged unique-index values on Modified commands would always be safe to skip, without considering that reassigning a 1:1 relationship with a unique index to an already-attached entity could cause the unchanged value to be a placeholder that later conflicts when the dependent's foreign key is updated.
why_it_breaks: The fix skips creating unique-index predecessor edges for Modified commands when the index value hasn't changed between original and current values. However, this overlooks the case where a 1:1 relationship is reassigned to an already-attached entity: the dependent's shadow foreign key may retain its original unchanged unique-index value while the relationship target changes, causing SaveChanges to emit an INSERT/UPDATE that violates the unique constraint on the new target. The agent assumed unchanged values are always benign, but here the unchanged value is a stale reference that becomes invalid after the relationship reassignment.

evidence.quote: The reported failure is a false circular-dependency detection when saving multiple entities that use a unique, store-generated clustering key alongside a composite key. In this shape, update command ordering treated unchanged unique-index values as conflicting dependencies and produced a cycle.
if (command.EntityState == EntityState.Modified) { var (currentValue, _) = rowIndexValueFactory.CreateEquatableIndexValue(command); if (Equals(value, currentValue)) { continue; } }
